reason: Membrane fats appear to form the boundary needed to enclose the cell fluid.
expectation: The fats should form a membrane around the fluid.

effect: The fats enclosed the fluid, but the picture shows no protein channels yet.
reaction: The missing channels give me a clear next step.
reason: Transport proteins appear suited to making the boundary selective.
expectation: The proteins should add channels to the membrane.

effect: The transport proteins completed the selective boundary, and the model now needs stored instructions and ATP machinery.
reaction: The picture clearly connects the channels with selective transport.
reason: DNA stores instructions, and the nuclear envelopes appear suited to enclosing it.
expectation: The DNA should be enclosed in nuclei that can provide stored instructions for the cell model.

effect: The DNA and envelopes formed muscle nuclei, which appear to fit the stored-instructions slot.
reaction: The porous membranes connect the nuclei to the earlier description of RNA leaving them.
reason: The nuclei contain the stored DNA instructions the muscle-cell model needs.
expectation: The nuclei should fill the stored-instructions slot.

effect: The nuclei are installed in the model; the oxygen-using ATP machinery is still needed.
reaction: The inset connects the stored DNA with copies passing through nuclear pores.
reason: Mitochondria are the cell structures associated with oxygen-using ATP production.
expectation: The mitochondria should fill the oxygen-using ATP machinery slot.

effect: The mitochondria are installed, and the next goal is to make pulling proteins and their structures.
reaction: The fuel, oxygen and ATP diagram makes the mitochondria’s role clearer.
reason: The opening says RNA building blocks use DNA in the nuclei to make a copy of the muscle-protein instructions.
expectation: The installed nuclei should provide a DNA template for an RNA copy.

alternatives.reason: I could check whether the building blocks interact directly with the model.

effect: The RNA copy is available, and the picture shows it traveling to a ribosome while the DNA stays in the nucleus.
reaction: The picture makes the division between stored DNA and the traveling copy clear.
reason: The copied instructions are meant to guide ribosomes in making the pulling proteins.
expectation: The ribosomes should use the RNA instructions to make muscle pulling proteins.

effect: The ribosomes used the copied instructions to make pulling protein threads, while the RNA and ribosomes remain intact.
reaction: The two panels make the connection between protein production and organized filaments clear.
reason: The muscle-cell model needs pulling structures, and the new threads appear to provide them.
expectation: The threads should be installed as pulling structures in the model.

effect: The threads completed the muscle fibers. The final picture adds that the repeating units shorten as filaments overlap further, while the filaments themselves keep their length.
reaction: That distinction was a satisfying final detail; it made the pulling structure easier to imagine.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the RNA copy and using it at ribosomes was the most worthwhile passage. The pictures connect stored DNA, a traveling copy and the production of pulling proteins in a clear sequence.

leastWorthwhile.text: Installing the nuclei was fairly predictable once the stored-instructions slot appeared, though the pore inset helped connect it to the later RNA step.

surprise.text: The final picture changed my understanding of shortening: the filaments overlap further without themselves getting shorter.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly arbitrary. The mitochondria choice drew on prior biology knowledge, but the result explained their role in remaking ATP.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because building from molecular instructions to a working muscle structure made me curious how the fibers will become tissues and contribute to a body system.
